tasks.short: Assess legislation, arbitration decisions and collective agreements for reward implications and industry trends.

steps.what: Collect relevant legislation, arbitration decisions and collective agreements.
Read sources and annotate changes against previous provisions.

loop.input: Retrieved source versions and previous provisions.
loop.output: Change register with quotations, source locations, jurisdiction and effective dates.
loop.check: Verify quotations and document versions mechanically; flag missing dates and conflicting provisions for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per document; unresolved entries remain flagged for manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different document structures and narrative decisions prevent reliable field extraction with fixed rules alone.

steps.what: Judge applicability, legal uncertainty and implications for current reward policies.
Write a briefing on reward trends, required changes and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Reviewed change register and applicability assessment.
loop.output: Reward change brief separating confirmed obligations, proposals, trends and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a source location for each legal assertion and preserve uncertainty from the assessment.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported assertions are removed or returned to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful narrative must connect varied provisions with the manager's contextual assessment.

steps.what: Discuss the briefing and agree investigation or policy-change priorities.

tasks.design: Configure source subscriptions and version storage in {DOCS}; use a scheduled job on {DATA_PLATFORM} for sources without suitable alerts. Bounded extraction and drafting loops produce cited change records and briefings, while managers decide applicability and approve actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources differ in format, jurisdiction and status. Automated summaries could obscure whether a provision actually applies.
tasks.enabler_now: Version comparison and source monitoring are established techniques. AI coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded text extraction can prepare cited records for review.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting interpretations, incomplete arbitration access and national rules still require specialist judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish an interesting industry development from a binding obligation and judge when legal advice is needed.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting documents to resolving applicability and proposing responses. Formal policy approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Agreement scope, arbitration precedent and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Source monitoring, version comparison and cited text extraction can support reward-policy research; applicability remains contextual.
The digest identifies reward answer desks and bounded document work as plausible building blocks, without a documented case for this complete workflow.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The source list is curated and collection respects access rights.
Research outputs do not automatically amend policies or employee records.
Build ranges cover a limited source set; consultation under national rules is assessed before rollout.
unknowns: Applicable countries, collective agreements and arbitration sources.
Available subscriptions, reuse rights and source interfaces.
Who can approve policy changes and when legal counsel must review.
Access lead times and any consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Which sources provide dependable version histories and effective dates?
How accurately does extraction distinguish adopted provisions from proposals on a representative document sample?
new_work: Review cited changes and resolve uncertain applicability.
Maintain source coverage and jurisdiction tags.
Repair failed collection and remove superseded interpretations.

tasks.short: Plan and deliver new-employee orientation, including reward policies, benefits and organisational objectives.

steps.what: Identify incoming employees and their orientation requirements.
Arrange sessions, facilitators and invitations.
Adapt approved orientation materials to the cohort's benefits and employment arrangements.
Welcome employees, explain objectives and benefits, and discuss their questions.
Answer outstanding questions and refer individual benefit issues to the appropriate specialist.

loop.input: Employee question and access-authorised passages from approved policies.
loop.output: Cited draft answer or specialist referral.
loop.check: Require current policy citations; escalate unclear eligibility, personal advice and conflicting provisions.
loop.stop: One retrieval and one draft per question; insufficient evidence produces a referral.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions use varied language and may combine several policy topics.

steps.what: Record attendance and send reminders for outstanding orientation requirements.

tasks.design: Configure {HCM}, {LMS} and {CALENDAR} to organise cohorts, invitations and completion records. A template generator assembles approved content from {DOCS}, and a bounded answer desk drafts cited follow-up answers for approval; the welcome and discussion remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Starter data, scheduling and benefit materials sit in different places. Cohort variations create repeated preparation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and scheduling features handle much of the administration. Small integrations and template generators are cheaper to build, while bounded drafting can assist follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, sensitive personal questions and explaining difficult benefit trade-offs depend on a knowledgeable person.
tasks.human_edge: Make employees comfortable asking questions and notice when a standard explanation has not met their needs.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling packs and arranging sessions, freeing capacity for benefits discussions. No additional pay or eligibility decision rights are implied.

reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible facilitation and checks of understanding.

evidence.claim: Cohort enrolment, scheduling, template assembly and completion tracking are established configurable or deterministic workflows.
The documented HR service case illustrates the importance of preserving access to people during service automation; it does not establish orientation savings.

assumptions: The manager delivers the reward portion of orientation within a wider HR programme.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates.
Approved content can be selected by explicit cohort and eligibility rules.
Only necessary employee data enters the workflow; GDPR and applicable national consultation rules are assessed.
unknowns: Which role owns orientation scheduling and attendance.
Available enrolment, calendar and employee-record interfaces.
Required languages, accessibility arrangements and cohort sizes.
Access approvals and whether employee consultation is required under national rules.
research_questions: Which existing enrolment and reminder features already cover the workflow?
Which question types can be answered from approved policies without individual advice?
new_work: Maintain approved content blocks and eligibility mappings.
Review draft answers and handle personal or ambiguous questions.
Resolve missing starter data and failed invitations.
Check that employees can still reach a person easily.

tasks.short: Prepare personnel budgets covering staffing, pay, benefits and other HR operating costs.

steps.what: Export staffing, payroll actuals and personnel operating costs.
Reconcile extracts and map employees and costs to budget categories.
Agree hiring, pay, benefits and timing assumptions with budget owners.
Calculate budget scenarios and explain movements against the baseline.
Challenge trade-offs and approve personnel spending limits.
Load the approved budget and distribute cost-centre reporting views.

tasks.design: A governed calculation service on {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles extracts from {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {ERP}, then generates scenarios from versioned assumptions. Budget owners approve assumptions and finance approves spending limits through {WORKFLOW}; only the approved version loads into {ERP} and feeds {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent cost mappings, manual extracts and changing assumptions made shared workbooks difficult to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Calculation rules and reconciliations need no model. AI coding lowers the effort of building connectors, scenario calculations and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Vacancy timing, collective agreement changes, employer charges and affordability remain uncertain. Country-specific payroll rules require maintained inputs.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible staffing and reward trade-offs and challenge assumptions that hide workforce pressure.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling files and rebuilding scenarios, and more time challenging workforce assumptions. Delegated spending authority remains unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile payroll movements and employer costs.
reach.learn: Payroll cut-offs, retroactive adjustments and reconciliation controls.

reach.task: Translate staffing plans into affordable workforce options.
reach.learn: Vacancy assumptions, organisational constraints and scenario interpretation.

evidence.claim: Personnel cost reconciliation and scenario calculations can use deterministic rules without a model loop.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with significant effects; budget calculation does not itself authorise individual pay decisions.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one budgeting scope.
Existing budgeting features are checked before custom calculations are built.
The solution forecasts costs; it does not change individual pay or staffing records.
Loads require an approved version, reconciled totals and duplicate protection.
GDPR access controls apply; consultation under national rules depends on the deployment's scope.
unknowns: Existing budgeting capabilities and available interfaces.
Countries, payroll calendars, employer charges and collective agreement coverage.
Quality of cost-centre and employee mappings.
Approval limits, data access lead times and required employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing budget configuration support the required scenario rules?
Which historical adjustments cause the largest baseline reconciliation differences?
Can a prior approved budget be reproduced from frozen inputs and assumptions?
new_work: Maintain cost rules and effective dates.
Review scenario assumptions and explain material forecast movements.
Monitor approved-version loading and access permissions.

tasks.short: Prepare, negotiate and formalise collective bargaining agreements.

steps.what: Collect current agreements, bargaining claims and workforce evidence.
Cost bargaining options and test alternative implementation dates.
Set the negotiation mandate, limits and escalation conditions.
Negotiate proposals and trade-offs with employee representatives within the mandate.
Draft agreement amendments and record unresolved wording.

loop.input: Current agreement, human-confirmed provisional terms and negotiation notes.
loop.output: Draft amendments with redlines and links to each confirmed term.
loop.check: Match every substantive amendment to a confirmed term; check dates, amounts and defined terms mechanically.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; ambiguous or unsupported wording becomes an open issue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiated prose requires contextual amendments across clauses; templates alone cannot reliably resolve wording dependencies.

steps.what: Review legal wording and confirm consistency with the employer's mandate.
Complete employee-side ratification under the applicable bargaining procedure.
Approve final employer commitments and execute the agreement with the counterpart.

tasks.design: A restricted workspace in {DOCS} and {CLM} assembles bargaining evidence, while deterministic calculations on {DATA_PLATFORM} generate cost scenarios. A bounded drafting loop prepares traceable amendments; people retain the mandate, negotiation, legal review and ratification, with approved execution through {ESIGN}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bargaining depends on relationships and contingent concessions. Evidence preparation and costing were often bundled with that human work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable cost calculations and controlled document assembly can separate preparation from negotiation. Bounded drafting can produce reviewable redlines without authority to make commitments.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, bargaining leverage, disputed interpretations and national rules remain central. Model drafting can subtly change obligations.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, understand interests behind claims and choose concessions that preserve a workable relationship.
tasks.altitude: The manager brings better-prepared evidence and faster cost options to bargaining, with less document assembly. Negotiating authority and signature rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare bargaining strategy and manage collective disputes.
reach.learn: Mandate design, bargaining procedure, national rules and dispute escalation.

reach.role: compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Model the distributional effects of proposed pay terms.
reach.learn: Pay-rule modelling, cohort analysis and checks for unequal effects.

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly and bargaining cost calculations can be deterministic while negotiation remains human.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent can apply to pay and job-evaluation systems, subject to collective-agreement exceptions; other national rules must be checked separately.
The digest provides no documented collective-bargaining case establishing savings for this proposed workflow.

assumptions: The employer participates directly in bargaining rather than only implementing a sector agreement.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates.
Ratification and signature sequences are adapted to the applicable national rules and bargaining procedure.
GDPR controls restrict bargaining data; union membership data receives special-category protection where present.
Access and consultation ranges estimate working effort; actual waiting periods may extend delivery.
unknowns: Whether bargaining occurs at employer or sector level.
Applicable countries, agreements, mandates and ratification procedures.
Permitted access to confidential bargaining records and any special-category data.
Employee consultation requirements and actual approval lead times.
Whether existing cost models and agreement version controls can be reused.
research_questions: Which negotiated terms can be costed with existing deterministic rules?
Can a drafting trial preserve every obligation and flag all unsupported amendments?
Which evidence may be shared with employee representatives, and at what aggregation?
new_work: Maintain cost rules and validate scenario inputs.
Review redlines for changed or unsupported obligations.
Maintain confidential access, version history and approval records.
Translate signed terms into reviewed implementation requirements.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward interpreting reward changes, testing workforce trade-offs and holding consequential conversations. Policy, budget and bargaining decisions remain with authorised people; faster preparation creates room for more frequent reviews.
reach: Labor relations specialists: collective agreement interpretation, bargaining procedure and dispute escalation.
Training and development specialists: accessible orientation and checks of understanding.
Payroll and timekeeping clerks: payroll reconciliation and effective-date controls.
Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists: cost modelling and distributional analysis.
skills_to_grow: Translate reward policies into explicit, testable calculation rules.
Validate source citations, document versions and model-drafted amendments.
Interpret workforce cost scenarios and challenge assumptions.
Apply GDPR controls and recognise when national consultation rules apply.
Facilitate sensitive benefit and bargaining conversations.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a monthly reward decision service combining vacancy-and-pay forecasts, weekly policy-change triage and first-month benefits clinics, using shared evidence and human-approved decisions.
